newsitem.title: LATVIA: BALTICS-MARKET WATCHDOGS DISCUSS PAN-BALTIC BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: BALTICS-MARKET WATCHDOGS DISCUSS PAN-BALTIC BOURSE.

text.p: The Latvian securities commission (LSC) said on Friday that it is in talks with its Estonian counterpart on adopting a common strategy towards merging the Baltic stock markets.

The two sides are considering a document which foresees future integration of the Baltic stock markets and their eventual merger with a larger market, Viktors Gustsons, the LSC chairman, told a news conference.
"There is no doubt whatsoever about the need for us (Baltic bourses) to merge into a single market as soon as possible," Gustsons said.
"Without excessive diplomacy one can say that for the time being it is just a matter of surviving," he added.
"Estonians are very loyal (to the idea), while Lithuanians are still thinking and they do not have a clear view on it," Gustsons said.

"We will continue talks on a letter of intent with the Estonian Department of securities on July 3 and hope to enter similar negotiations with the Lithuanian securities commission in September," Gustsons said.
"The Baltic securities market will exist but as an addition to a bigger market," Gustsons added.
"It is an open question whether the bourse, depository and regulatory institutions will be situated here," he said.
Gustsons said that both the size of the Baltic market and costs involved in maintaining separate bourses are major issues.
Small countries would find it hard to finance complicated information systems which provide speed and security for transactions, Gustsons said.
"We will have American experts arriving in September to work on the Baltic market integration model," Gustsons said.
The state supervising bodies of the securities markets of the three Baltic states have decided to meet every three months to discuss co-ordination matters.

The planned letter of intent also includes issues of joint training, drawing on foreign expertise through expert help and the introduction of international bookeeping and auditing standards, as well work on harmonising trading systems.
